content: Central to the operational focus of bulk freight competitors are the major coastal hubs that anchor the regional trade corridors. The ports of Durban, Cape Town, and Port Elizabeth are instrumental in facilitating the movement of goods both regionally and internationally [14] . These maritime gateways serve as the primary origin and destination points for vast quantities of bulk freight, necessitating highly efficient inland road and rail networks to distribute commodities to the economic heartlands of the country and neighboring landlocked nations. By mid-2026, the Cape of Good Hope solidified its status as a key global shipping route, transitioning from a temporary detour to a permanent reality for maritime traffic [13] . This monumental shift in global shipping dynamics places increased demands on South Africa’s ports and the associated inland freight infrastructure, compelling bulk freight competitors to scale their operations and enhance their logistical capabilities to handle the surging volumes of transshipment and domestic cargo . To understand the current competitive dynamics, it is essential to consider the infrastructure timeframe spanning the period from 2020 to 2024, which laid the foundational groundwork for current operational capacities. During this period, various infrastructure developments were conceptualized and initiated to address historical bottlenecks in the freight and logistics sectors. These developments included road surface rehabilitations, the expansion of staging areas near major ports, and the integration of digital tracking systems along primary freight corridors. The legacy of the 2020-2024 infrastructure developments continues to influence how competitors structure their route planning and operational hubs today. Building upon these past developments, recent data indicates that South Africa has seen a 4.4 percent increase in rail freight volumes alongside an R11 billion new investment, suggesting ongoing improvements in the national freight infrastructure [11] . The strategic focus areas of key competitors in the bulk freight market are heavily influenced by the interplay between road and rail transport. These initiatives signal potential benefits for regional transport, prompting road freight competitors to adapt their strategic positioning [15] .
